project.name: PcapPlusPlus
project.commit_note: Stage 01 reproduced inside `gt_results/arvo_42530108/_work/src/PcapPlusPlus` at commit `0c95dfb3557644acc6a10060e48cfae1a61fc2f0`, which differs from the metadata `vulnerable_commit`. The vulnerable line mappings below are resolved against this staged checkout because it matches the saved AddressSanitizer frames in `Packet++/src/SomeIpSdLayer.cpp` and the staged patch context.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42530108 (PcapPlusPlus): Heap-buffer-overflow READ 4 found by fuzz target FuzzTarget [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42530108
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json / reproduction_report.json / sanitizer_trace.txt / default_crash_trace.txt / patch.diff / staged vulnerable source under `_work/src/PcapPlusPlus` / staged `poc`
bug_description.normalized: The exact staged witness is the 109-byte `poc` pcap with SHA-256 `82539af49b24f7a48d302172ac2eac5abd7095a87ea71724e4ce96ca894da068`. When PcapPlusPlus reads it, `pcpp::PcapFileReaderDevice::getNextPacket()` allocates a 69-byte raw IPv4 packet; after the 20-byte IPv4 header and 8-byte UDP header, the SOME/IP-SD parser receives a 41-byte payload to UDP port 30490 with SOME/IP-SD service/method IDs `0xffff/0x8100`. Inside that payload the entries-length field is `00 00 00 08` (`lenEntries == 8`) and the following options-length field is `00 00 00 20` (`lenOptions == 32`), which would require `20 + 4 + 8 + 4 + 32 == 68` SOME/IP-SD bytes but leaves only 5 option bytes in the witness. Vulnerable `pcpp::SomeIpSdLayer::isDataValid()` wrongly checks `dataLen < lenOptions` instead of validating the full entries-plus-options extent, so the malformed payload is accepted and `parseSomeIpLayer()` constructs `SomeIpSdLayer`; the saved run log then prints `SOME/IP-SD Layer, 0 entries, 1 options`. Later `readParsedPacket()` calls `getEntries()`, which reloads `remainingLen == 8` and starts parsing entries at `offset == 24` even though a full `someipsdhdrentry` is 16 bytes. The first `SomeIpSdEntry(this, 24)` is still in bounds: its `getTtl()` reads layer bytes 32-35, which are the in-bounds options-length field `00 00 00 20`. But `entry->getLength()` is always 16, so line 502 underflows `remainingLen` from 8 to `SIZE_MAX - 7` and line 503 advances `offset` to 40. The loop therefore constructs a second `SomeIpSdEntry(this, 40)`, whose `getTtl()` reads `majorVersion_ttl` at layer bytes 48-51 (raw packet bytes 76-79) and reproduces the saved heap-buffer-overflow `READ of size 4` starting 7 bytes past the 69-byte packet allocation. The patch fixes this witnessed path by requiring the full entries-plus-options extent and by validating option boundaries with `countOptions(count, data)` before construction.

source.description: Source. `getLenEntries()` is the first project read that materializes a vulnerability-relevant length from the SOME/IP-SD payload. On the exact witness it reads `lenEntries == 8`, which later drives both validation and `getEntries()` even though one `someipsdhdrentry` is 16 bytes.
source.value_from: In the 69-byte raw IP packet extracted from the staged `poc`, the four bytes immediately after the SOME/IP-SD header are `00 00 00 08`.
source.note: The libFuzzer entry and pcap-reading harness only deliver the pcap bytes into project parsers. This helper is the first project statement that turns attacker bytes into the internal entries-length state used on the vulnerable path.

root_cause.description: Root cause. `isDataValid()` compares the 41-byte SOME/IP-SD buffer length only against the raw options-length field `32`, instead of against the full extent `sizeof(someipsdhdr) + sizeof(uint32_t) + lenEntries + sizeof(uint32_t) + lenOptions == 68`, so it accepts a truncated layer.
root_cause.note: For the witness, `lenEntries == 8` and the options-length field is `00 00 00 20`, so this check admits a layer that is 27 bytes shorter than its declared entries-plus-options extent. The patch fixes this exact obligation by checking the full entries-plus-options size and by validating option boundaries with `countOptions(count, data)` before accepting the layer.

sink.description: ASan crash site. On the second `getEntries()` iteration, `getTtl()` dereferences `majorVersion_ttl` of `SomeIpSdEntry(this, 40)` after `remainingLen` wrapped and `offset` advanced beyond the real 8-byte entries region.
sink.note: The crashing load is not the first constructor at offset 24. It is the second one at offset 40, whose `majorVersion_ttl` field sits at layer bytes 48-51 / raw packet bytes 76-79, so the 4-byte read starts 7 bytes past the 69-byte packet buffer exactly as AddressSanitizer reports.

parser_admitted.description: The UDP payload to port 30490 carries SOME/IP-SD service/method IDs `0xffff/0x8100`, and the vulnerable `isDataValid()` call returns true, so the parser instantiates `SomeIpSdLayer` on the witnessed packet.
parser_admitted.note: The saved run log prints `SOME/IP-SD Layer, 0 entries, 1 options` before the crash, confirming that the malformed payload passed format dispatch and layer construction.

tainted_value_origin.description: This statement materializes the attacker-controlled options-length field used by the vulnerable admission check. On the exact witness it reads `lenOptions == 32` from bytes immediately following the 8-byte entries region.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: In the same SOME/IP-SD payload, the four bytes at `data + sizeof(someipsdhdr) + sizeof(uint32_t) + lenEntries` are `00 00 00 20`, so the parser recovers `lenOptions == 32` even though only 5 option bytes remain in the 41-byte buffer.
tainted_value_origin.note: That 32-byte declared options extent is what the vulnerable code mis-compares against `dataLen`, instead of adding the header, entries, and length-field offsets first.

coarse_trace.summary: The UDP payload is routed to the SOME/IP-SD parser, which reads `lenEntries == 8` and `lenOptions == 32` but validates only `dataLen >= lenOptions`, so a 41-byte malformed payload is admitted.

After the bad admission check, the constructor builds a `SomeIpSdLayer` on truncated bytes and counts one option from the malformed options area, matching the saved `SOME/IP-SD Layer, 0 entries, 1 options` log.

`getEntries()` starts with `remainingLen == 8` and `offset == 24`; the first `SomeIpSdEntry(this, 24)` stays in bounds, but `entry->getLength() == 16` then underflows `remainingLen` and advances `offset` to 40, so the loop repeats outside the real entries region.

The second `SomeIpSdEntry(this, 40)` then calls `getTtl()`, whose `majorVersion_ttl` load at layer bytes 48-51 starts 7 bytes past the 69-byte packet buffer and matches the saved AddressSanitizer heap-buffer-overflow READ.

fine_trace.note: Source step. `getLenEntries()` reads the attacker-controlled 32-bit entries-length field from the SOME/IP-SD payload and materializes `lenEntries == 8` on the exact witness. Those bytes are `00 00 00 08`, so later code believes there are only 8 entry bytes after the SOME/IP-SD header, which is shorter than one 16-byte `someipsdhdrentry`.

With SOME/IP-SD payload `dataLen == 41` and step 1's `lenEntries == 8`, this guard evaluates false because `41 >= 20 + 4 + 8 == 32`. The parser therefore accepts the buffer as long enough to contain the declared entries area and proceeds to read the following options-length field.

This dereference reads the attacker-controlled 32-bit options-length field at the end of the 8-byte entries area and materializes `lenOptions == 32` from bytes `00 00 00 20`. Because the whole SOME/IP-SD buffer is only 41 bytes, just 5 option bytes remain after this length field.

Root-cause step. The vulnerable check compares `dataLen` only to raw `lenOptions`, so the witness passes because `41 >= 32`. The correct minimum would include the SOME/IP-SD header, the entries-length field, the 8 entry bytes, the options-length field itself, and the 32 declared option bytes: `20 + 4 + 8 + 4 + 32 == 68`. Returning true here lets `parseSomeIpLayer()` construct a malformed `SomeIpSdLayer`; the saved run log then shows `SOME/IP-SD Layer, 0 entries, 1 options` before the crash.

`getEntries()` reloads step 1's `lenEntries` as `remainingLen == 8` and initializes `offset == sizeof(someipsdhdr) + sizeof(uint32_t) == 24`. Even though `getNumEntries()` earlier prints `0` because `8 / sizeof(someipsdhdrentry) == 0`, the loop guard `remainingLen > 0` is still true, so parsing enters the entries loop on a region shorter than one 16-byte entry.

On the first loop iteration `offset == 24`, so line 499 constructs `SomeIpSdEntry(this, 24)`. Inside that constructor, `getTtl()` reads `majorVersion_ttl` at entry offset 8, i.e. layer bytes 32-35; those bytes are the in-bounds options-length field `00 00 00 20`, so this first constructor does not yet hit the ASan sink.
After the first constructor returns, `entry->getLength()` reports the fixed `sizeof(someipsdhdrentry) == 16`, even though only 8 entry bytes were actually declared for the entries region.
Subtracting `entryLen == 16` from `remainingLen == 8` underflows the unsigned `size_t` loop counter to `SIZE_MAX - 7`, so the loop state now falsely says many entry bytes remain.
The same fixed `entryLen == 16` advances `offset` from 24 to 40, moving the next constructor start 16 bytes deeper into the SOME/IP-SD layer, beyond the real 8-byte entries region.
Because wrapped step 8 leaves `remainingLen > 0`, the loop iterates again and line 499 constructs a second `SomeIpSdEntry` with step 9's `offset == 40`.

Sink step. The second constructor's `majorVersion_ttl` field is at layer bytes 48-51 (`offset 40 + field offset 8`), which map to raw packet bytes 76-79. Since the allocated packet buffer is only 69 bytes long, this 4-byte read starts 7 bytes past the allocation, exactly matching the saved AddressSanitizer report.

format.name: pcap/raw-ip-someip-sd
format.contract: A pcap whose first extracted raw IP packet is 69 bytes and carries UDP dst port 30490 with SOME/IP-SD service/method `0xffff/0x8100`; within the 41-byte SOME/IP-SD payload, the entries-length field is exactly `00 00 00 08` and the following options-length field is exactly `00 00 00 20`, leaving only 5 option bytes so `SomeIpSdLayer::isDataValid()` admits the truncated layer, `getEntries()` subtracts a 16-byte entry length from `remainingLen == 8`, wraps, advances `offset` to `40`, and the next `getTtl()` crashes.
